note: 'Now the parable is this: The seed is the word of God' (Luke 8:11). The clearest kind of key there is: the speaker of the parable explaining it in the next breath.

'And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God' (Eph 6:17). The verse keys itself, and neither half of it could be stored until the word had a record and the sword had one.

'For the word of God is living and active. Sharper than any double-edged sword, it pierces even to dividing soul and spirit' (Heb 4:12) -- the same pair arriving from the other direction. Ephesians says the sword is the word; Hebrews says the word is sharper than a sword. The two verses share only 'the word of God', which occurs 47 times and is far too common to link them by wording, so nothing but these two edges puts them side by side.
